summary: Your coral-reef imaging mission is coherent and supported by STK screenshots, with a clear mission need and single-spacecraft rationale. However, core orbital values (Kourou latitude, SSO inclination), contact-duration claims, EOL analysis and referencing need correction. You are at Adequate for C2/C3/C4 and low Accomplished for C1; the next level requires accurate, well-supported and professionally presented evidence.
next_steps: Correct the orbital-mechanics values and claims: Kourou latitude (~5.2°N, not 45.05°N), 600 km SSO inclination (~97.8°, not 87.79°), RAAN justification using launch geometry, and mean contact duration (580.786 s, not almost 20 min). Update affected figures and text.
Add a quantitative end-of-life/deorbit analysis (including 25-year/space-debris compliance) and include the required STK/PIGI software files so your design evidence is complete.

Improve presentation and referencing: number and caption all figures/tables, replace bare URLs and Wikipedia with properly formatted citations matching the reference list, and explicitly identify the operator and customers in the Introduction.

criteria.C1: Your Introduction clearly explains the coral-reef imaging need and why one spacecraft suffices, with mostly appropriate references. To move beyond low Accomplished, explicitly identify the operator and customers (not just implied scientists) and add specific detail on their roles. That will meet the Accomplished requirement for detailed descriptions and appropriate literature.
criteria.C2: You cover all major design areas and include STK screenshots, but key values undermine accuracy: Kourou is ~5.2°N not 45.05°N; 600 km SSO inclination should be ~97.8° not 87.79°; mean contact is 580.786 s (9.7 min), not almost 20 min. Justify RAAN with launch geometry, add quantitative deorbit/25-year compliance, and include required STK/PIGI files. Accomplished requires accurate, comprehensive, persuasive evidence.
criteria.C3: Your Conclusion summarises the design and notes launch-vehicle uncertainty, but it largely restates earlier sections and inherits the orbit/coverage errors. To reach Accomplished, draw specific conclusions from corrected evidence—e.g., quantified coverage, contact frequency and EOL compliance—rather than repeating the body. Keep the launch-risk point but tie it to design impact.
criteria.C4: You use clear headings and an executive summary, making the report readable. To reach Accomplished, number and caption all figures/tables consistently, replace bare URLs and Wikipedia with properly formatted references that match in-text citations, and polish spelling/grammar and language style. The current presentation is Adequate but not yet professional.
